metadata.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

problem_summary.summary: Map each digit from 2 through 9 to its phone-keypad letters and return every string formed by choosing one letter per digit.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a digit string. Return all corresponding letter strings; the result may be in any order.
constraints: Each digit is in the range '2' through '9'

brute_force.explanation: Expand a list of partial strings one digit at a time. For each partial string, copy it once per letter on the next key and append that letter. This straightforward breadth-by-position approach materializes intermediate strings at every depth.
brute_force.correctness_idea: After processing a prefix of digits, the list contains exactly the strings formed by all choices for that prefix. Expanding by every letter on the next key extends each partial choice exactly once.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(L * P) — P is the number of returned strings and L is the number of digits; intermediate string construction copies prefixes.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(P * L) for the returned strings, plus O(P * L) peak intermediate strings.

optimized.explanation: Use depth-first backtracking with one mutable StringBuilder. At each position, try each mapped letter, recurse to the next digit, then remove the letter before trying the next choice.
optimized.correctness_idea: At recursion depth i, the builder contains one choice for each of the first i digits. Trying every letter for digit i explores every possible extension, and restoring the builder keeps sibling branches independent.
optimized.time_complexity: O(L * P) — all P output strings have length L and must be materialized.
optimized.space_complexity: O(L) auxiliary for the builder and recursion stack, excluding O(P * L) output.

steps.event: Choose the first letter for digit 2.
steps.condition: index is before the final digit.
steps.action: Append a and recurse to index 1.

steps.event: Try each letter for digit 7 under prefix a.
steps.condition: Each of p, q, r, s is a valid choice.
steps.action: Append each choice at the leaf, record it, and backtrack.

steps.event: Backtrack and choose b for digit 2.
steps.condition: The a branch has been fully explored.
steps.action: Append b and explore digit 7 choices.

steps.event: Explore c, then finish the root choices.
steps.condition: No more letters remain after c.
steps.action: Record cp, cq, cr, cs and return the 12 strings.

edge_cases.handling: Returns an empty list rather than a list containing an empty string.
Returns each letter on that key as a one-character string.
Their four-letter mappings are included, so output size reflects those larger branches.
